plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies, since you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $43, I will bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' actions. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to bid below or above my true valuation of $8. Bidding higher risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $8 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the highest competing bid, and I pay only the second-highest bid, guaranteeing non-negative profit when I win and no risk of overpaying. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down in this format.
